title: How the model of the atom changed

draft.title: How the model of the atom changed
card: A model of the atom is changed when new evidence does not fit the old one. Scientists have updated the model several times.
He found the electron, a tiny negative particle inside the atom. So atoms were not solid balls that could not be split.
His team fired positive particles at thin gold foil. Most went straight through, but a few bounced back. This showed a small, dense, positive nucleus with mostly empty space around it.
He found the neutron, a particle in the nucleus with no charge. This explained why the nucleus has more mass than its protons alone.
draft.remember: New evidence changed the model: electron, then nucleus, then neutron.

a.q: In the gold foil experiment, a few particles bounced back. What did this show?
opts: Atoms have a small, dense nucleus
Atoms are solid balls of gold
a.why: Only a small, dense, positive centre could push particles back. Most passed straight through because the atom is mostly empty space. The electron was found earlier, in Thomson's work.
a.clue: Think about what could be hard enough to bounce a particle back.

b.q: Before 1932, scientists could not explain why atoms weigh more than their protons add up to. Which discovery fixed this?
opts: Chadwick found neutral particles in the nucleus
Thomson found negative particles in the atom
Rutherford found that atoms are mostly empty space
Rutherford found that the nucleus is positive
b.why: Neutrons have mass but no charge, so they add mass to the nucleus without changing its charge. Thomson's electrons are very light, so they could not account for the missing mass.
b.clue: Which particle adds mass but has no charge?

a.best: Atoms have a small, dense nucleus

b.best: Chadwick found neutral particles in the nucleus
